outputs.L3:
The battery module includes a plurality of battery cells, each having electrode leads, and a connection member configured to electrically connect the battery cells to one another.

The plurality of battery cells are divided into a first battery group and a second battery group. The battery cells in each of the first and second battery groups are arranged side by side in a first direction. The second battery group is disposed so that the electrode leads of the battery cells in the second battery group face the electrode leads of the battery cells in the first battery group.

The connection member is positioned between the first battery group and the second battery group. The electrode leads of the battery cells in both groups are connected to the connection member, thereby establishing electrical connection between the battery cells.

In particular, with respect to battery cells that face each other across the connection member, an electrode lead of a battery cell in one group is brought into contact with one surface of the connection member, while an opposing electrode lead of a battery cell in the other group is brought into contact with the other surface of the connection member. Accordingly, the connection member is interposed between the facing electrode leads and serves to electrically connect the corresponding battery cells in a compact and reliable manner.
outputs.L4:
A battery module is disclosed that includes a plurality of battery cells arranged in two groups facing each other. The battery cells in each group may be stacked or aligned in a predetermined direction, and each battery cell includes electrode leads extending toward a space formed between the two facing groups. A connection member is disposed in this space between the opposing battery cell groups and is configured to electrically connect the electrode leads of the battery cells.

In particular, electrode leads extending from battery cells of one group are brought into contact with an upper surface of the connection member, while electrode leads extending from battery cells of the opposite group are brought into contact with a lower surface of the connection member. The connection member may be formed as a conductive plate, bus bar, or similar electrical connection element capable of electrically coupling the electrode leads of the facing battery cells. The electrode leads may be joined to the connection member by welding, soldering, mechanical fastening, or another suitable bonding method.

Because the electrode leads from the two facing groups are connected to opposite surfaces of the same connection member, the battery module can reduce the number of separate connection components required for electrical interconnection. This arrangement also allows the battery cells to be positioned more compactly, thereby improving space utilization within the module. In addition, since the electrode leads are supported and connected at both the upper and lower surfaces of the connection member, the electrical connection between the battery cells can be made more stable and reliable.

The disclosed structure is particularly advantageous in battery modules requiring a high degree of integration, such as modules used in electric vehicles, energy storage systems, power tools, or other devices requiring high-capacity rechargeable batteries. By arranging the battery cells in two facing groups and positioning the connection member between them, the module can achieve efficient current flow, simplified assembly, reduced wiring complexity, and improved mechanical stability of the electrical connections.

Accordingly, the battery module provides an effective connection structure in which electrode leads of facing battery cells are electrically connected through a shared connection member. This configuration enhances module layout efficiency, improves connection reliability, and supports the manufacture of compact, high-performance battery modules.

**Disclosed**

The word **“disclosed”** refers to something that has been revealed, made known, or shared openly. It is often used when information that was previously private, hidden, or confidential becomes available to others. In business, law, finance, and communication, disclosure plays an important role in building trust and transparency.

For example, a company may disclose financial details to investors so they can make informed decisions. In legal situations, important evidence or documents may be disclosed to ensure fairness. In personal relationships, disclosing information can help create honesty and understanding.

However, not all information should be disclosed without careful consideration. Sensitive data, such as personal details, medical records, or confidential business plans, must be protected and shared only when appropriate. Responsible disclosure means revealing information in a way that is ethical, legal, and respectful of privacy.

Overall, being disclosed means that information has moved from being unknown or hidden to being openly available. Whether in professional settings or everyday life, disclosure can support accountability, clarity, and informed decision-making.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a battery module where two opposing groups of battery cells have electrode leads connected to opposite surfaces of a connection member between them.
counterfactuals.output: A battery module includes a first cell group and a second cell group disposed to face each other, each cell group including a plurality of battery cells having electrode leads extending toward a region between the first and second cell groups. A connection member is disposed between the first cell group and the second cell group and includes a first surface facing the first cell group and a second surface opposite the first surface and facing the second cell group. Electrode leads of the first cell group are electrically coupled to the first surface of the connection member, and electrode leads of the second cell group are electrically coupled to the second surface of the connection member. The connection member thereby electrically connects the battery cells while reducing lead overlap and enabling a compact module structure with simplified assembly and improved electrical connection reliability.

counterfactuals.output:
In one embodiment, an energy storage module includes a plurality of battery cells arranged in a first cell group and a second cell group disposed side-by-side. The first cell group and the second cell group are oriented such that electrode lead portions of the battery cells in the first cell group face electrode lead portions of corresponding battery cells in the second cell group.

A connection member is disposed between the first cell group and the second cell group. The connection member may be configured as a busbar or busbar-like conductive member having a first major surface and an opposite second major surface. Electrode leads of the battery cells of the first cell group are electrically connected to the first major surface of the connection member, and electrode leads of the battery cells of the second cell group are electrically connected to the second major surface of the connection member. Accordingly, the electrode leads of the two cell groups may be connected to opposite surfaces of the same connection member, thereby providing a compact electrical connection structure between the facing cell groups.

1. A battery module comprising:  
   a first group of battery cells;  
   a second group of battery cells disposed adjacent to the first group of battery cells, the first group and the second group being arranged such that electrode leads of the first group face electrode leads of the second group; and  
   a conductive connection member disposed between the first group and the second group, the conductive connection member comprising a first surface facing the first group and a second surface opposite the first surface and facing the second group,  
   wherein electrode leads of the first group are electrically connected to the first surface of the conductive connection member, and electrode leads of the second group are electrically connected to the second surface of the conductive connection member.

2. The battery module of claim 1, wherein the conductive connection member comprises a busbar.

3. The battery module of claim 1, wherein the electrode leads of the first group and the electrode leads of the second group are connected to the conductive connection member by welding.

4. The battery module of claim 1, wherein the first group and the second group are arranged in parallel rows on opposite sides of the conductive connection member.

5. The battery module of claim 1, wherein the conductive connection member electrically connects at least one battery cell of the first group to at least one battery cell of the second group.

6. The battery module of claim 1, wherein the electrode leads of the first group overlap the first surface of the conductive connection member and the electrode leads of the second group overlap the second surface of the conductive connection member.

counterfactuals.prompt: Provide a patent-style description of a battery module structure in which a first battery group and a second battery group are arranged so their electrode leads face each other and are connected to a connection member located between them.
counterfactuals.output:
A battery module structure is provided. The battery module structure may include a battery cell assembly comprising a first battery group and a second battery group arranged adjacent to each other. Each of the first battery group and the second battery group may include a plurality of battery cells, each battery cell having an electrode lead protruding from at least one side thereof.

The first battery group and the second battery group may be disposed such that electrode leads of the first battery group and electrode leads of the second battery group face each other. A connection member may be positioned in a space between the first battery group and the second battery group. The electrode leads of the first battery group and the electrode leads of the second battery group may be electrically connected to the connection member.

In one embodiment, the connection member may extend in a longitudinal direction of the battery module and may include one or more conductive portions configured to electrically interconnect selected electrode leads of the first battery group and selected electrode leads of the second battery group. The connection member may function as a bus bar, an interconnection plate, or a terminal connecting member for forming a series and/or parallel electrical connection between the battery cells.

The electrode leads of the first battery group may extend toward the second battery group, and the electrode leads of the second battery group may extend toward the first battery group. The respective electrode leads may be bent, overlapped, welded, bonded, or otherwise joined to the connection member. The connection member may be arranged substantially centrally between the first battery group and the second battery group, thereby reducing an overall wiring length and improving spatial efficiency of the battery module.

In some embodiments, an insulating member may be disposed between the connection member and portions of the battery cells other than the electrode leads. The insulating member may prevent unintended electrical contact between the connection member and cell bodies of the first and second battery groups. The connection member may include a plurality of connection regions separated by insulating portions, each connection region corresponding to one or more electrode leads.

The battery module structure may further include a module housing accommodating the first battery group, the second battery group, and the connection member. The housing may include a support portion for positioning the first battery group and the second battery group such that the electrode leads face each other with a predetermined gap therebetween. The connection member may be received in the gap and fixed relative to the housing.

According to this structure, because the electrode leads of the first and second battery groups face inwardly toward each other and are connected to a connection member disposed therebetween, the battery module may have a compact configuration. In addition, the length of conductive paths may be reduced, resistance may be lowered, heat generation may be reduced, and assembly of the electrode leads to the connection member may be simplified.
